title: Answer: no account of what consciousness is, only that it is fixed by the present state

statements.text: The theorem takes no position on what consciousness is. It constrains where any account must look: under local state sufficiency and causal efficacy, consciousness at a time is fixed by the complete present physical state of the system, $C_t = f(X_t)$, and not by what the system has done. Which property of that state constitutes experience is left as the remaining task. The closing perspective, that mind may be a state of matter and matter a state of mind, is offered as a view and not as a result.
statements.scope: the no-go theorem, version 1 of the preprint

sources.quote: Consciousness is due not to what a system has done, but what it is.
The remaining task is therefore to identify which property of the present physical state constitutes experience.
perhaps mind is a state of matter, and matter is a state of mind.
